exposure: Adnexal masses ≥5 cm in diameter removed at cesarean delivery
cohort: The study included 60 women who underwent removal of an adnexal mass ≥5 cm during cesarean delivery, matched with 120 randomly selected control women who underwent cesarean delivery without mass removal.
finding: Removal of an adnexal mass ≥5 cm in diameter during cesarean operation is not associated with increased composite obstetric morbidity, mean drop in hematocrit, postoperative fever, or postpartum hospitalization, but it does result in a longer operative length.
followup_time: Until postpartum hospital discharge (approximately 2.4-2.5 days post-operation)
